  }
  .entry-meta .byline { 
    grid-area: author; 
    display: block; 
    width: 100%;
  }

  /* 3e ligne : ★ à gauche, temps de lecture à droite */
  .entry-meta a.meta-item { grid-area: rating; }
  .entry-meta span.meta-item { grid-area: readtime; }

  /* Optionnel : taille/espacement un peu plus confortables */
  .entry-meta .posted-on time,
  .entry-meta .byline,
  .entry-meta .meta-item { line-height: 1.3; }
}

/*FIN LEGEND IMAGE UNE */</style><script>// Attendre que le DOM soit entièrement chargé avant d’exécuter le script
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {

  // Fonction qui rend un élément entier cliquable
  const handleLinkClick = function (e) {
    // Vérifie si la cible du clic n’est PAS un lien
    if (!e.target.href) {
      // Trouve le premier <a> à l’intérieur de l’élément cliqué et simule un clic
      this.querySelector("a").click();
    }
  };

  // Fonction qui gère les clics sur les éléments avec un attribut [data-goto]
  const handleGotoClick = function (e) {
    // Décoder l’URL encodée en Base64 stockée dans l’attribut data-goto
    const goto = window.atob(this.dataset.goto);

    // Si l’utilisateur fait Ctrl+clic, Cmd+clic ou si data-external est présent
    if (e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey || this.dataset.external) {
      // Ouvre le lien dans un nouvel onglet
      window.open(goto, "_blank", "noopener").focus();
    } else {
      // Sinon, redirige la page actuelle vers le lien
      window.location.href = goto;
    }
  };

  // Liste des éléments WordPress à rendre entièrement cliquables
  const expandClickElements = [
    ".wp-block-latest-posts > li",         // Liste d’articles récents
    ".generate-columns-container > article", // Articles dans GeneratePress
    ".gb-query-loop-item",                 // Élément de boucle de requête
    ".gb-loop-item",                       // Élément de boucle
    ".wp-block-post-template > .wp-block-post", // Template de posts
    ".site-branding-container",            // Zone de branding (logo, titre)
  ];

  // Pour chaque sélecteur, rendre les éléments concernés cliquables
  expandClickElements.forEach((selector) => {
    document.querySelectorAll(selector).forEach((el) => {
      el.addEventListener("click", handleLinkClick, { passive: true });
    });
  });

  // Pour tous les éléments avec l’attribut [data-goto],
  // ajouter un événement de clic qui applique la logique de redirection
  document.querySelectorAll("[data-goto]").forEach((el) => {
    el.addEventListener("click", handleGotoClick, { passive: true });
  });

});
</script><link rel="license" href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/deed.fr">

<article id="post-10217" class="post-10217 post type-post status-publish format-standard has-post-thumbnail hentry category-news" itemtype="https://schema.org/CreativeWork" itemscope>
	<div class="inside-article">
					<header class="entry-header">
				<h1 class="entry-title" itemprop="headline">Google taps MediaTek for upgraded Triggerfish AI chip with 3x memory boost</h1>		<div class="entry-meta">
			<span class="posted-on"><time class="entry-date published" datetime="2026-06-22T10:17:43-04:00" itemprop="datePublished">Published on 22 June 2026 at 10:17 am</time></span><span class="meta-separator" aria-hidden="true"> &bull; </span><span class="byline"><span class="author vcard" itemtype="http://schema.org/Person" itemscope="itemscope" itemprop="author">Written by <a class="url fn n" href="https://eciks.org/author/chris-martin" title="View all posts by Chris Martin" rel="author"><span class="fn n author-name" itemprop="name">Chris Martin</span></a></span></span><span class="meta-separator" aria-hidden="true"> &bull; </span><span class="meta-item">Reading duration : 2 minutes</span> <span class="o50">&middot;</span> <span class="meta-item">read 80 times</span>		</div>
					</header>
			<figure class="featured-image" style="view-transition-name: transition-10216;"><img width="896" height="597" src="https://eciks.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/60513-google-taps-mediatek-for-upgraded-triggerfish-ai-chip-with-3x-memory-boost.jpg-scaled.png" class="attachment-large size-large wp-post-image" alt="Google taps MediaTek for upgraded Triggerfish AI chip with 3x memory boost" elementtiming="hero-image" fetchpriority="high" decoding="async" /><figcaption>&copy; Google taps MediaTek for upgraded Triggerfish AI chip with 3x memory boost</figcaption></figure><div class="component"><div class="component share-buttons-toggler"><button class="button button-native" data-share-url="native"><svg aria-hidden="true" focusable="false" class="icon icon-share" width="24" height="24"><use xlink:href="#icon-share"></use></svg>Share this post</button></div><div class="component social-share"><span class="button button-facebook" data-share-url="facebook"><svg aria-hidden="true" focusable="false" class="icon icon-facebook" width="24" height="24"><use xlink:href="#icon-facebook"></use></svg> Post<span class="hide-on-mobile"> on Facebook</span></span><span class="button button-flipboard" data-share-url="flipboard"><svg aria-hidden="true" focusable="false" class="icon icon-flipboard" width="24" height="24"><use xlink:href="#icon-flipboard"></use></svg> Post<span class="hide-on-mobile"> on Flipboard</span></span><span class="button button-linkedin" data-share-url="linkedin"><svg aria-hidden="true" focusable="false" class="icon icon-linkedin" width="24" height="24"><use xlink:href="#icon-linkedin"></use></svg> Share<span class="hide-on-mobile"> on LinkedIn</span></span><span class="button button-reddit" data-share-url="reddit"><svg aria-hidden="true" focusable="false" class="icon icon-reddit" width="24" height="24"><use xlink:href="#icon-reddit"></use></svg> Post<span data-share-url="whatsapp"><svg aria-hidden="true" focusable="false" class="icon icon-whatsapp" width="24" height="24"><use xlink:href="#icon-whatsapp"></use></svg> Send<span class="hide-on-mobile"> through Whatsapp</span></span></div></div>
		<div class="entry-content" itemprop="text">
			<p>Google is tapping MediaTek as the exclusive partner for an upgraded tensor processing unit codenamed Triggerfish, marking a significant expansion of the Taiwanese chipmaker&#8217;s role in Google&#8217;s AI infrastructure strategy. The enhanced TPU v9 variant features two to three times the SRAM capacity of its base Humufish design and integrates next-generation HBM4E memory, according to supply chain analyst Ming-Chi Kuo and multiple industry sources confirmed on June 22, 2026.</p><div class='code-block code-block-4' style='margin: 8px 0; clear: both;'>
<!-- CODE 1 eciks.org -->
<ins class="adsbygoogle"
     style="display:block"
     data-ad-client="ca-pub-8509871116631275"
     data-ad-slot="2326719974"
     data-ad-format="auto"
     data-full-width-responsive="true"></ins>
<script>
     (adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({});
</script></div>

<p>The Triggerfish chip is optimized for AI agent inference and reinforcement learning workloads, two emerging priorities in the AI industry. By nearly tripling the on-chip SRAM&#8212;the processor&#8217;s fast, immediate-access memory&#8212;the design allows more active workloads to remain on-chip, reducing the need to fetch data from slower external memory pools. This architecture addresses a critical bottleneck in AI computing known as the &#8220;memory wall,&#8221; where data movement between memory levels becomes the limiting factor in performance.</p>
<p>Google&#8217;s TPU strategy has evolved significantly over the past year. The company now spreads development across four major partners: Broadcom, MediaTek, Marvell, and Intel, each handling specialized roles in training and inference tasks. MediaTek already contributes to Google&#8217;s TPU v8 inference models, so Triggerfish represents an escalation rather than a new relationship. The Taiwanese chipmaker is moving from a supporting player to a critical node in Google&#8217;s AI infrastructure supply chain.</p><div class='code-block code-block-1' style='margin: 8px 0; clear: both;'>
<!-- CODE 2 eciks.org -->
<ins class="adsbygoogle"
     style="display:block"
     data-ad-client="ca-pub-8509871116631275"
     data-ad-slot="1843126940"
     data-ad-format="auto"
     data-full-width-responsive="true"></ins>
<script>
     (adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({});
</script></div>

<p>Production of Triggerfish is scheduled to begin in late 2027, with volume ramping through 2028. Google projects lifetime shipments of 1 to 2 million Triggerfish units, compared to 4 to 5 million units for the standard Humufish TPU v9. The incremental order carries an approximately 30% increase in unit pricing versus the base Humufish design, a notable shift from Google&#8217;s prior TPU v8 strategy, which targeted a 20 to 30% reduction in costs.</p>
<p>The HBM4E memory standard underpinning Triggerfish represents the latest advance in high-bandwidth memory technology. Samsung shipped the first 12-layer HBM4E samples in May 2026, with speeds reaching 16 gigabits per second and a more than 20% improvement in bandwidth over its HBM4 predecessor, according to Reuters and industry reports.</p>
<p>Analyst projections suggest MediaTek will account for approximately 25% of all AI ASIC server compute shipments by 2028, a dramatic expansion from its historical role. This deal underscores Google&#8217;s broader strategy to diversify its custom silicon supply chain and reduce reliance on any single partner, particularly as demand for AI infrastructure accelerates across the industry.</p><div class='code-block code-block-3' style='margin: 8px 0; clear: both;'>
<!-- CODE 3 eciks.org -->
<ins class="adsbygoogle"
     style="display:block"
     data-ad-client="ca-pub-8509871116631275"
     data-ad-slot="4341297771"
     data-ad-format="auto"
     data-full-width-responsive="true"></ins>
<script>
     (adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({});
</script></div>

<h3>Sources</h3>
<ul>
<li><strong>Crypto Briefing</strong> &#8212; Triggerfish chip specifications, SRAM capacity, HBM4E integration, production timeline, shipment projections, pricing premium, four-supplier strategy, and MediaTek&#8217;s 25% market share projection</li>
<li><strong>Yahoo Finance</strong> &#8212; Triggerfish memory upgrade details, HBM4E support, workload targeting, and SRAM capacity benefits</li>
<li><strong>Reuters</strong> &#8212; HBM4E speed and bandwidth specifications</li>
</ul>
